FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Cytogenetics and Molecular Pathology

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Clinical Indication: Presentation myeloma
Diagnosis: Multiple myeloma

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase and metaphase FISH analysis for multiple myeloma panel

PROBE SETS UTILIZED
1. IGH Break Apart Probe (14q32)
2. IGH/FGFR3 Dual Color Dual Fusion Probe t(4;14)(p16.3;q32)
3. 1q21/1p36 Dual Color Probe
4. CLL Panel including:
   - ATM (11q22.3)
   - TP53 (17p13.1)
   - D13S319/13q34 (13q14/13q34)
5. Multi-color Probe Set for Chromosomes 5, 9, and 15

RESULTS

INTERPHASE FISH ANALYSIS (100 nuclei scored per probe set):

IGH/FGFR3 Rearrangement:
- POSITIVE: IGH/FGFR3 fusion signals detected in 33/100 cells (33%)
- Consistent with t(4;14)(p16.3;q32) rearrangement

Chromosome 13 Status:
- ABNORMAL: Loss of both 13q14 and 13q34 signals in 58/100 cells (58%)
- Pattern consistent with monosomy 13

1q21/1p36 Analysis:
- 1q21: GAIN detected - Three signals in 26/100 cells (26%)
- 1p36: NORMAL - Two signals in all cells analyzed

ATM (11q22.3):
- DELETION detected in 38/100 cells (38%)

TP53 (17p13.1):
- NORMAL: Two signals in all cells analyzed

Chromosomes 5, 9, and 15:
- NORMAL: Two signals for each chromosome in all cells analyzed

METAPHASE FISH ANALYSIS:
50 metaphase cells analyzed
- No abnormalities detected in dividing cells

INTERPRETATION
This FISH analysis reveals multiple chromosomal abnormalities characteristic of high-risk multiple myeloma:

1. The IGH/FGFR3 rearrangement t(4;14) detected in 33% of cells is associated with poor prognosis in multiple myeloma. This translocation results in dysregulation of FGFR3 and MMSET, contributing to myeloma pathogenesis.

2. Monosomy 13 (loss of entire chromosome 13) identified in 58% of cells is a common finding in multiple myeloma and may confer additional adverse prognostic significance when combined with t(4;14).

3. Gain of 1q21 in 26% of cells represents an additional high-risk feature associated with disease progression and shorter survival.

4. ATM deletion detected in 38% of cells may impact DNA damage response pathways.

The absence of abnormalities in metaphase cells suggests that the malignant plasma cells have low proliferative activity, which is typical for multiple myeloma.

These findings indicate a high-risk cytogenetic profile that should be considered in treatment planning and prognostic assessment.

Reported by: [redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Reviewed by: [redacted name], M.D., Director of Cytogenetics
